title: Shift laws for both prescribed completed tensor slots
statement: Fix a prime ell, a finite extension E/Q_ell and a scheme W. Use the actual ambient completed-coefficient derived category and its completed tensor, defined by the quotient tensor tower, products and Cone(1-s)[-1] [def-pur-integral-operation-complex-models]. The two prescribed natural tensor-slot shifts [def-pur-integral-operation-shift-data], normalized on every good flat-term K-flat pair by the unsigned first-slot formula, the coefficient (-1)^(ri) second-slot formula and the cone formula (b,a) mapped to (b,(-1)^r a), extend in each individual slot to a coherent integer CommShift structure. There are families of CommShift structures on the two partial completed tensor functors whose components at all derived objects and all integers are exactly the prescribed integralLeft and integralRight comparison components. In particular these maps satisfy the zero/addition equations for integer shifts, with their existing naturality in both arguments.

source.place: Definition cone (Tag 014E), together with homology.tex 011G, derived.tex 0941 and parent proof Steps 5 and 6.

proof.text: Construct the two global addition comparisons by tensoring the input shift-addition natural isomorphism with the identity, whiskering the prescribed b- and a-comparisons in order, and applying inverse output shift addition. Restriction of functors to pairs of good complexes is fully faithful by the good resolving localization. Apply its injectivity to the component identities of completedTensorShift_add_on_good. This proves equality of global natural isomorphisms.

Restrict each global comparison to a partial tensor functor by NatIso.ofComponents. Its naturality follows by applying the original two-variable naturality to (f,id) or (id,f). The global addition identity becomes CommShift.isoAdd on each partial functor.

Derive the zero law from addition at (0,0), without a separate representative zero lemma. Compare isoAdd(s_0,s_0)=s_0 with isoAdd(isoZero,s_0)=s_0. On each component cancel the mapped input shift-addition isomorphism, s_0 at the shifted input, and inverse output shift addition. Faithfulness of shift by zero gives s_0=isoZero. Package the restricted comparisons and these zero/addition proofs as CommShift structures. Their components are definitionally the prescribed tensorShifts components.

F4: good-model addition is the one split-off step; fully faithful descent and the zero law are proved in Lean.

lean.statement:
theorem completedTensorSlotShiftLaws (W : Scheme.{u}) :
    ∃ (s₁ : ∀ N : Integral l E W,
            ((Functor.curry.obj (integralCompletedTensor l E W)).flip.obj N).CommShift ℤ)
          (s₂ : ∀ M : Integral l E W,
            ((Functor.curry.obj (integralCompletedTensor l E W)).obj M).CommShift ℤ),
          (∀ (M N : Integral l E W) (r : ℤ),
            (Functor.commShiftIso _ (self := s₁ N) r).app M =
              ((tensorShifts l E).integralLeft W r).app (M, N)) ∧
          (∀ (M N : Integral l E W) (r : ℤ),
            (Functor.commShiftIso _ (self := s₂ M) r).app N =
              ((tensorShifts l E).integralRight W r).app (M, N))
